questions.question_text: What four sights moved Prince Siddhartha to renounce his royal luxuries at age 25?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Prince Siddhartha was moved by encountering a sick man, an aged man, a funeral procession, and a begging monk, prompting him to seek enlightenment.

questions.question_text: What central thesis does W.B. Yeats present regarding physical vs divine love in 'For Anne Gregory'?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Yeats asserts that human suitors love women superficially for physical beauty (yellow hair), whereas only God possesses the capacity to love a person purely for their inner self.

questions.question_text: Why could Kisa Gotami not get mustard seeds from any household in Benares?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Buddha specified seeds must come from a home unblemished by death. Gotami found that every household had lost a parent, child, husband, or friend, proving death's universality.

questions.question_text: How does Anne Gregory suggest she can test whether suitors love her true self?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Anne suggests she can dye her yellow hair brown, black, or carrot so that men will be forced to look past external appearance and love her character alone.

questions.question_text: Explain the spiritual analogies of 'ripe fruits' and 'earthen vessels' used in Buddha's sermon.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Buddha compares mortals to ripe fruits in constant danger of falling, and to earthen vessels crafted by potters bound to break, illustrating that physical death is unavoidable.

questions.question_text: Why did Buddha send Kisa Gotami on an impossible quest instead of giving a lecture?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Buddha used experiential pedagogy, allowing Gotami to discover through her own search that death is universal, transforming her selfish grief into spiritual acceptance.

questions.question_text: According to Buddha, how can an individual pull out the 'arrow of lamentation' to achieve peace?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: An individual obtains peace of mind by surrendering weeping and selfish sorrow, realizing impermanence, and overcoming grief to become composed and blessed.

questions.question_text: What source did the speaker cite in 'For Anne Gregory' to prove divine love?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The speaker cited an old religious text declared by a holy man the previous night, proving that only God loves individuals for themselves regardless of physical features.

questions.question_text: Summarize the overarching message of 'The Sermon at Benares' for modern readers facing loss.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The sermon teaches that death is a natural universal reality. Weeping does not revive loved ones; true mental peace comes from accepting mortality and overcoming selfish grief.

questions.question_text: How does Yeats contrast human vanity with spiritual depth in 'For Anne Gregory'?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Yeats highlights how human attraction is easily swayed by external beauty (hair color), contrasting it with divine love which sees through physical vanity to embrace inner soul.
